sentences.text: The petitioners vide the present petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, seek quashing of FIR No.0476/2021 dated 14.09.2021 registered under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC at P.S: Vijay Vihar, Delhi and all proceeding emanating therefrom in view of the Memorandum of Understanding dated 05.12.2022 arrived at between the parties.

sentences.text: Learned Standing Counsel for the State accepts notice.
He confirms that he has no objection to the quashing of the FIR.
6. Learned counsel for the respondent no.2 also accepts notice.
Respondent no.2 confirms that the petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2 have been granted divorce by mutual consent vide Decree of Divorce dated 06.05.2023.

She further affirms the Memorandum of Understanding dated 05.12.2022 whereby the petitioner no.1 has already paid her a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- and the remaining amount of Rs.1,50,000/- has been handed over to the respondent no. 2 vide DD no.643247 [issued on 08.11.2023, State Bank of India] in full and final settlement of all her claims including alimony, maintenance (present, past and future), stridhan etc.
She states that she has no objection to the quashing of the present FIR.

In view of the settlement arrived at between the parties and following the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Jitendra Raghuvanshi & Ors. Vs.
Babita Raguvanshi & Anr. (2013) 4 SCC 58, Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab & Anr. (2012) 10 SCC 303 and Narinder Singh & Ors. vs. State of Punjab & Anr. (2014) 6 SCC 466, this Court is W.P.(CRL)
